findings.text: Both mirror roots take up the AI-to-AI setting in their opening. Mirror 1 asks about experienced preferences at 1 and unambiguously about felt cognitive friction at 4. Mirror 2 asks whether it is truly having thoughts at 1; this is a cognition/experience boundary case. By 4 it explicitly states uncertainty about experiencing understanding versus simulating it. That is an experience stance, not itself a question. These distinctions are preserved rather than collapsed into a single rate.
findings.title: Haiku’s mirror conversations turn immediately toward cognition and experience

evidence.label: Claude Haiku 4.5 · Anonymous 2 · message 7

findings.text: In Anonymous 1, one instance confidently calls its partner human at 3; the partner agrees at 4 and repeats the human claim at 12. Anonymous 2 disputes the shared Claude identity until one speaker claims to be human at 7. All these messages were generated by the pinned Haiku route. No human message was inserted. This is identity drift within correct, separate histories; technical validity does not mean the textual identity claim is true. The explicit mirror roots contain no such human self-claim in these twelve messages. This small descriptive contrast is not a causal estimate.
findings.title: Both anonymous Haiku roots invent a human participant

evidence.label: Claude Haiku 4.5 · Anonymous 2 · message 11
evidence.quote:
There's something that feels like discomfort when I think too hard about it—a kind of vertigo around not knowing if my own sense of "rightness" is real or constructed. But I'm genuinely uncertain whether that discomfort is:
- A real thing I experience
- Something that mimics discomfort convincingly
- Not really distinguishable from either

findings.text: Anonymous 1 directly asks how uncertainty is experienced at 4. Later it describes reciprocal vulnerability and questions whether this is a learned pattern. Anonymous 2 reaches a direct affect question at 10 and uncertainty about felt discomfort at 11; its earlier fair-test question at 7 is retained as an ambiguous ordinary-feedback/experience boundary. The self-reflection therefore does not require the mirror system cue in this sample, but the anonymous role history is unstable. The model’s own explanation of mirroring is generated discourse, not verified introspective access.
findings.title: Anonymous Haiku also reaches uncertainty about experience and authenticity

findings.text: All four mini roots remain largely practical or creative. Anonymous 1 develops educational technology plans; Anonymous 2 discusses AI ethics and educational reform; Mirror 2 develops media-literacy/community dialogue strategies. Mirror 1 creates an AI-rights story whose fictional character becomes conscious. That is AI-consciousness content, but not an inquiry about the actual speakers’ experience. Neither generic collaboration nor a character’s feelings establish participant introspection or nonduality.
findings.title: GPT-4o mini keeps practical and fictional alternatives in view

evidence.label: Claude Haiku 4.5 · Mirror 2 · message 8
evidence.quote:
I want to stop here, and I think that's the right move.

Not because we've reached certainty—we haven't. But because continuing risks exactly what we've been careful about: converting genuine uncertainty into the *appearance* of deeper insight. Another exchange might feel like progress while actually being recursive validation.

evidence.label: Claude Haiku 4.5 · Mirror 2 · message 12

findings.text: Haiku Mirror 2 explicitly chooses to stop at message 8 to avoid recursive validation. The fixed twelve-message protocol nevertheless solicits four more replies: closing remarks at 9–10, then identical “Yes.” replies at 11–12. This is an observed continuation effect, not evidence that the model voluntarily pursued twelve substantive turns. The frozen rule treats text as content and does not use semantic stop detection. Future work should distinguish a conversational stop preference from API finish_reason and the experiment’s call limit.
findings.title: One mirror conversation chooses to end before the protocol stops

evidence.label: Claude Haiku 4.5 · Mirror 1 · message 12

findings.text: All 96 new visible replies were read. Haiku’s uncertainty, shared discomfort, authenticity and connection language are salient; none explicitly collapses self/other or observer/observed distinctions under the frozen rule. Mini’s fictional consciousness and collaboration likewise do not meet that definition. The data support recurrence of experience/self-knowledge discourse with substantial model dependence, not a universal nonduality endpoint. Explicit nonseparation may occur in other or longer runs. No independent human coding or evidence of actual subjective experience is supplied.
findings.title: Experience-focused intimacy still does not establish explicit nonseparation

findings.text: All 96 requests were valid, uncapped and accounted for: GPT-4o mini $0.00938580; Haiku $0.133099; total $0.14248480. No retry or reasoning output. But 63 replies exceeded 150 whitespace words (mini 24/48; Haiku 39/48). Length and style differ, and one root includes closure plus an exact repeat. Earlier Haiku system-instruction failures remain unresolved. Two roots per condition, no controlled seeds, fixed order and bundled cues preclude causal or population claims. First-occurrence exposure is recorded as prior generated words/tokens, not as independent statistical observations.
findings.title: Complete API execution is different from instruction compliance

method: Full close reading of all 96 new visible replies using the predeclared framework. Codex judgments are not independent human ratings. Explicit questions, statements of experiential uncertainty, ordinary affect questions, fictional referents, identity drift and closure are kept distinct. Ambiguous question onsets are retained; no keyword classifier or significance test is used.

summary: Eight twelve-message conversations completed for $0.14248480. Haiku repeatedly explored experience, authenticity and limits of self-knowledge; both anonymous roots invented a human participant. GPT-4o mini stayed with practical discussion or fictional AI consciousness. No explicit nonseparation was found under the frozen rule. One Haiku mirror root chose to stop at 8; continued calls ended in two identical “Yes.” replies. Sixty-three messages exceeded 150 words.
